Bug_Title: Classes should not be compared by name
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the code by comparing objects by their class name. The bug is also present in the code that checks if a class is assignable from List.class.
Trigger_Explanation: The existing test codes are calling methods that use class names to determine object types, which is a violation of the bug rule. The test codes should be updated to use the instanceof operator or the Class.isAssignableFrom() method instead.
Model_Explanation: The described bug is present in the code. The code is comparing classes by name, which can lead to security issues. The noncompliant code example shows that the class name 'Pear' is being compared, which can lead to unexpected behavior if a malicious user sends an object of the same name as the trusted class. The compliant solution uses the instanceof operator or the Class.isAssignableFrom() method to check the object’s underlying type, which prevents this issue.
